title: Measuring Inference: TTFT, TPOT, Throughput and Goodput
summary: Before you can make a model faster or cheaper you have to measure it the way users feel it. This lesson splits a request into its phases, defines time to first token, time per output token and end-to-end latency, and shows why percentiles and goodput tell you more than averages and raw throughput.
objectives: Break a streamed LLM request into network, queue, prefill and decode time and compute TTFT, TPOT and end-to-end latency
Compute p50, p95 and p99 from a sample of latencies and explain why the mean misleads
Distinguish throughput from goodput and compute goodput under a latency SLO
Translate a product experience (chat, voice, batch jobs) into concrete latency targets
Design a benchmark that produces trustworthy serving numbers
prerequisites: You should know what prefill and decode are and why generation happens one token at a time ([Context Windows, Prefill and the KV Cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache)), and what a token is ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)). No serving experience is assumed.
